rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extending the gaze means prolonging it and holding it in admiration of what is seen.
rows.anchor: ومد النظر تطويله وأن لا يكاد يرده استحسانا للمنظور إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passing, unextended glance is excused: one may first notice something, then lower the gaze.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن النظر غير الممدود معفو عنه وذلك أن يبادر الشيء بالنظر ثم بغض الطرف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan warns against admiring the ostentation of profligates and urges seeing the humiliation of disobedience upon them.
rows.anchor: حتى قال الحسن لا تنظروا إلى دقدقة هما ليج الفسقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ostentatious possessions are displayed to attract onlookers; gazing at them rewards and encourages their owners to keep displaying them.
rows.anchor: إنما اتخذوا هذه الاشياء لعيون النظارة فالناظر إليها محصل لعرهم ومغر لهم على اتخاذها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enjoyment is given to classes among the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أصنافا من الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwājan may be an accusative circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in the verb, with the verb applying to them: some of them, or people among them.
rows.anchor: ويجوزان ينصب حالا من هاء الضمير والفعل واقع على منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zahrat al-ḥayāt al-dunyā means the world's adornment and splendor.
rows.anchor: زينتها وبهجتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zahratan is accusative as blame, as an apposition to what they were given, or as an apposition to classes with an implied possessors of splendor.
rows.anchor: وانتصب على الذم وعلى ابداله محل به أو على ابداله من ازواجا على تقدير ذوي زهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense is that God tests them through it until their ingratitude makes them deserve punishment.
rows.anchor: لنبلوهم حتى يستوجبوا العذاب لوجود الكفران منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means that God will punish them in the afterlife because of it.
rows.anchor: أو لتعذبهم في الآخرة بسببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's provision can mean His reward, namely Paradise.
rows.anchor: ثوابه وهو الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means lawful, sufficient sustenance.
rows.anchor: أو الحلال الكافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's provision is better and more enduring than the worldly goods people received.
rows.anchor: ﴿ خير وأبقى ﴾ فما رزقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahlak may mean your community.
rows.anchor: أمتك أو أهل بيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means your household.
rows.anchor: أمتك أو أهل بيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is commanded to keep his household or community at prayer and personally persist in it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بالصلاة واصطبر ﴾ أنت داوم ﴿ عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not ask the Prophet to provide for himself or his family; God provides for them, so he should focus on worship and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي لا نسألك ان ترزق نفسك ولا اهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi adds that whoever is occupied with God's work is cared for by God.
rows.anchor: لأن من كان في عمل الله كان الله في عمله

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: When he saw what the rulers possessed, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr recited the preceding warning against coveting worldly goods, then called people to prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن عروة بن الزبير أنه كان إذا رأى ما عند السلاطين فرأ ولا تمدن عينيك الآية ثم ينادي الصلاة الصلاة

rows.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله المزني
rows.claim: When his family faced hardship, Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzanī told them to rise and pray, citing God's command.
rows.anchor: وكان بكر بن عبد الله المزني إذا أصاب أهله خصاصة قال قوموا فصلوا بهذا أمر الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report in some musnads, related from Malik ibn Dinar, says the Prophet ordered his family to pray and recited this verse when hardship struck them.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار مثله في بعض المسانيد انه عليه السلام كان اذا اصاب اهله ضرا أمرهم بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that the good outcome belongs to the Godfearing, with two annexed nouns elided.
rows.anchor: أي وحسن العاقبة لأهل التقوى بحذف المضافين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqtaraba means to draw near.
rows.anchor: ﴿ اقترب ﴾ دنا ﴿ للناس ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is an extra connective particle with iqtaraba.
rows.anchor: اللام صلة لاقترب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the people meant are the polytheists, since the following descriptions concern them.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن المراد بالناس المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their account is the time when God reckons with them and requites them for their deeds: the Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: وقت محاسبة الله إياهم ومجازاته على أعمالهم يعني يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day is called near because little remains compared with what has passed, and everything that is coming is near.
rows.anchor: لقلة ما بقي بالاضافة إلى ما مضى ولأن كل آت قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are heedless of their reckoning and fate, and turn away from preparing for that Day.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهم في غفلة ﴾ عن حسابهم وعما يفعل بهم ثم ﴿ معرضون ﴾ عن التأهب لذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general nearness applies to all, but heedlessness varies: some are absorbed in worldly life and away from God, awakening only at death; others are absorbed in God and away from the world, awakening only at the vision of the Lord.
rows.anchor: فالاقتراب عام والغفلة والاعراض يتفاوتان بتفاوت المكلفين فرب غافل عن حسابه لاستغراقه في دنياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi urges self-accounting before being judged, alertness before being summoned, avoidance of the heedless, and remembrance of the Creator.
rows.anchor: فالواجب عليك ان تحاسب نفسك قبل أن تحاسب وتتنبه للعرض قبل ان تنبه

rows.speaker: خزاعة
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Khuzaʿa, who said that the angels were God's daughters.
rows.anchor: نزلت في خزاعة حيث قالوا الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above the claim that He has a child; the angels are honored, exalted, and brought near servants, not offspring, since servitude contradicts parentage.
rows.anchor: فنزه ذاته عن ذلك ثم أخبر عنهم بأنهم عباد بقوله ﴿ بل عباد مكرمون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise is the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ﴿ واقترب الوعد الحق ﴾ أي القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to idha is idha hiya, with sudden idha; sudden idha can stand in place of the fa in a recompense clause.
rows.anchor: وجواب اذا ﴿ فإذا هي ﴾ وهي إذا المفاجأة وهي تقع في المجازاة سادة مسد الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When fa is also included after idha, the two particles jointly connect the answer to its condition and reinforce the link; the wording could instead say fa-hiya shakhisa or idha hiya shakhisa.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاءت الفاء معها تعاونتا على وصل الجزاء بالشرط فيتأكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun hiya is indefinite or ambiguous until explained by al-absar.
rows.anchor: وهي ضمير مبهم يوضحه الابصار ويفسره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' eyes are fixed with lids raised, scarcely blinking from the terror they experience.
rows.anchor: ﴿ شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا ﴾ أي مرتفعة الأجفان لا تكاد تطرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclamation depends on an omitted verb meaning they say; the saying is circumstantial of the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يا ويلنا ﴾ متعلق بمحذوف تقديره يقولون يا ويلنا ويقولون حال من الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers to the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قد كنا في غفلة من هذا ﴾ اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They confess to wrongdoing by putting worship in a place where it did not belong.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بل كنا ظالمين ﴾ بوضعنا العبادة في غير موضعها

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi argues that doubters should consider their first creation: humans began as soil and fluid, and their objection to resurrection is only that the created being becomes soil and fluid again.
rows.anchor: يعني أن ارتبتم في البعث فمزيل ريبكم أن تنظروا في بدء خلقكم وقد كنتم في الابتداء قرابا وماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We created you from dust refers to creating your father, Adam, from dust.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فإنا خلقناكم ﴾ أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alaqa is a piece of clotted blood.
rows.anchor: أي قطعة دم جامدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mudgha is a small piece of flesh about the size of what is chewed.
rows.anchor: أي لحمة صغسيرة قدر ما يمضغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formed embryo is smooth and free of deficiency or defect.
rows.anchor: المخلقة المسواة الملساء من النقصان والعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Embryos differ: some are fully formed and smooth, others deficient; this variation yields differences in people's forms, stature, height, and completeness.
rows.anchor: يخلق المضغ متفاوته منها ما هو كامل الخلقة أملس من العيوب ومنها ما هو على عكس ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages display God's complete power and wisdom and prove His ability to restore what He initiated, despite the dissimilarity of soil and fluid.
rows.anchor: بهذا التدريج كمال قدرتنا وحكمتنا وإن من قدر على خلق البشر من تراب أولا

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Everyone except al-Mufaḍḍal reads nuqirru in the nominative, beginning a new sentence after a pause.
rows.anchor: بالرفع عند غير المفضل مستأنف بعد وقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God retains in the womb whatever He wills to remain until the appointed time of birth; what He does not will to remain is miscarried.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ونقر ﴾ بالرفع عند غير المفضل مستأنف بعد وقف أى نحن نثبت ﴿ في الأرحام ما نشاء ﴾ ثبوته ﴿ إلى أجل مسمى ﴾ أي وقت الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tiflan is circumstantial and can be a generic singular, or the wording can mean that each of you is brought out as a child.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم نخرجكم ﴾ من الرحم ﴿ طفلا ﴾ حال واريد به الجنس فلذا لم يجمع أو اريد به ثم نخرج كل واحد منكم طفلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase implies that God raises you until you reach the fullness of your intellect and strength.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم لتبلغوا ﴾ ثم نربيكم لتبلغوا ﴿ أشدكم ﴾ كمال عقلكم وقوتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd is a plural form with no singular used for it.
rows.anchor: وهو من الفاظ الجموع التي لا يستعمل لها واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some die upon reaching maturity, before it, or after it.
rows.anchor: عند بلوغ الأشد أو قبله أبو بعده

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most decrepit age means old age and senility.
rows.anchor: أخسه يعني الهرم والخرف

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of the sense is that an old person no longer knows anything after having known it.
rows.anchor: أي لكيلا يعلم شيئا من بعد ما كان يعلمه

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the person ceases to acquire knowledge and forgets what he once knew.
rows.anchor: أو لكيلا يستفيد علما وينسى ما كان عالما به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi introduces the reviving earth as a second proof of resurrection.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر دليلا آخر على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is dead and dry.
rows.anchor: ميتة يابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It moves with the vegetation, swells, and rises.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت ﴾ تحركت بالنبات ﴿ وربت ﴾ وانتفخت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj means a kind or species; bahij means beautiful and pleasing to those who see it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأنبتت من كل زوج ﴾ صنف ﴿ بهيج ﴾ حسن سار للناظرين إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address asks whether Muhammad knows with certainty as if he had seen it.
rows.anchor: ألم تعلم يا محمد علما يقوم مقام العيان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says all listed creation prostrates to God, though people cannot perceive it, just as they do not comprehend its glorification.
rows.anchor: قيل ان الكل يسجد له ولكنا لا نقف عليه كما لا نقف على تسبيحها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view calls the nonrational beings' compliance with God's acts and subjection to Him prostration, by analogy with the prostration of accountable beings.
rows.anchor: وقيل سمي مطاوعة غير المكلف له فيما يحدث من أفعاله وتسخيره له سجودا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many people prostrate to God in obedience and worship.
rows.anchor: أي ويسجد له كثير من الناس سجود طاعة وعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, kathīrun is a subject qualified by min al-nās, with its predicate omitted and understood from the following clause about reward.
rows.anchor: أو هو مرفوع على الابتداء ومن الناس صفة له والخبر محذوف وهن مثاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many people deserve punishment because of their disbelief and refusal to prostrate.
rows.anchor: وكثير منهم حق عليه العذاب بكفره وابائه السجود

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whom God disgraces through wretchedness have no one to honor them with felicity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن يهن الله ﴾ بالشقاوة ﴿ فما له من مكرم ﴾ بالسعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the Muʿtazilites, who say God wills things but does not do them, since it states that He does whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: ظاهر هذه الآية والتي قبلها ينقض على المعتزلة قولهم لانهم يقولون شاء اشياء ولم يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhina can be genitive as an apposition, accusative with an implied aʿni, or nominative with an implied hum.
rows.anchor: فى محل جر بدل من الذين أو نصب بأعنى أو رفع باضمارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people expelled from their homes are the believers expelled from Mecca.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أخرجوا من ديارهم ﴾ بمكة

words: بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were expelled without cause except their profession of God's oneness, which should have entitled them to remain, not caused expulsion; the phrase is a genitive apposition to haqq.
rows.anchor: بغير موجب سوى التوحيد الذى ينبغى أن يكون موجب التمكن لا موجب الاخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi compares the wording with the verse asking whether believers are resented for believing in God.
rows.anchor: ومثله هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا بالله

rows.speaker: مدني ويعقوب
rows.claim: Madinan and Yaqub read difaa, the verbal noun of mutual defense, in place of dafʿ.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولولا دفع الله ﴾ دفاع مدنى ويعقوب

rows.speaker: حجازى
rows.claim: The Hijazis read the verb with a light form.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الناس بعضهم ببعض لهدمت ﴾ وبالتخفيف حجازى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without Muslims being empowered to struggle against disbelievers, polytheists would dominate religious communities and demolish their houses of worship; alternatively, they would overrun Muslims and protected People of the Book and destroy both groups' worship places.
rows.anchor: أى لولا اظهاره وتسليطه المسلمين على الكافرين بالمجاهدة لا ستولى المشركون على أهل الملل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other worship places are named before mosques because they existed earlier or were closer to demolition.
rows.anchor: وقدم غير المساجد عليها لتقدمها وجودا أو لقربها من التهديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about frequent remembrance applies either only to mosques or to all the previously listed places of worship.
rows.anchor: فى المساجد أو فى جميع ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Helping God means helping His religion and His allies.
rows.anchor: أى ينصر دينه وأولياءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is strong enough to help His allies and mighty in taking vengeance on His enemies.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن الله لقوي ﴾ على نصرأوليائه ﴿ عزيز ﴾ على انتقام أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed a sacrificial rite for every religious community, refuting those who claim sacrifice is not part of God's law.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لكل أمة ﴾ أهل دين ﴿ جعلنا منسكا ﴾ من بيانه وهو رد لقول من يقول ان الذبح ليس بشريعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the ones who perform that rite.
rows.anchor: ﴿ هم ناسكوه ﴾ عاملون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not heed their argument or allow them to draw you into disputation.
rows.anchor: فلا يجادلنك والمعنى فلا تلتفت إلى قولهم ولا تمكنهم من أن ينازعوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matter in dispute may mean the sacrificial rites or the religion.
rows.anchor: أمر الذبائح أو الدين

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: The verse was revealed when polytheists challenged Muslims for eating animals they slaughtered but not carrion they said God had killed.
rows.anchor: نزلت حين قال المشركون للمسلمين ما لكم تأكلون ما قتلتم ولا تأكلون ما قتله الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to call people to worship his Lord.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وادع ﴾ الناس ﴿ إلى ربك ﴾ إلى عبادة ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is on an upright path.
rows.anchor: طريق قويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then We made him means his offspring, with the annexed noun omitted and its dependent taking its place; Adam himself did not become a drop of semen.
rows.anchor: أى نسله فحذف المضاف وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه لأن آدم عليه السلام لم يصر نطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi compares the wording to the account that human creation began from clay and then Adam's offspring came from a fluid extract.
rows.anchor: وهو كقوله وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the human to mean Adam's children and the extract to mean semen, which Arabs call sulala; it is extracted from clay in the sense of being from Adam, who was made from clay.
rows.anchor: وقيل الإنسان بنو آدم والسلالة النطفة والعرب تسمى النطفة سلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nutfa means a small amount of water.
rows.anchor: ماء قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarar is a place of rest, namely the womb; makin means secure or fortified.
rows.anchor: ﴿ في قرار ﴾ مستقر يعنى الرحم ﴿ مكين ﴾ حصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here khalaqna means made or transformed, since it takes two objects, unlike khalaqa in its usual sense, which takes one.
rows.anchor: أى صيرناها بدلالة تعديه إلى مفعولين والخلق يتعدى إلى مفعول واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alaqa is a piece of blood; the white semen becomes red blood.
rows.anchor: قطعة دم والمعنى أحلنا النطفة البيضاء علقة حمراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mudgha is flesh about the size of a chewed morsel.
rows.anchor: لحما قدر ما يمضغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The embryo is made into bones, then flesh is grown over them like clothing.
rows.anchor: فصيرناها عظاما ﴿ فكسونا العظام لحما ﴾ فأنبتنا عليها اللحم فصار لها كاللباس

rows.speaker: الشامي وأبو بكر وزيد عن يعقوب وأبو زيد
rows.claim: On the bones wording, Shami and Abu Bakr have the singular azman; Zayd from Yaqub reads the definite plural, while Abu Zayd has the definite singular, used for the plural without ambiguity because humans have many bones.
rows.anchor: العظم شامى وأبوبكر عظما العظام زيد عن يعقوب عظاما العظم عن أبى زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun can refer to the human being or to the thing just mentioned.
rows.anchor: الضمير يعود إلى الانسان أوإلى المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a distinct new creation: God makes a living animal from inanimate matter, with speech, hearing, and sight after their opposites.
rows.anchor: خلقنا مباينا للخلق الأول حيث جعله حيوانا وكان جمادا وناطقا وسميعا وبصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a usurped egg hatches while in someone's possession, the person owes the egg but does not return the chick, since it is a new creation distinct from the egg.
rows.anchor: إذا غصب بيضة فأفرخت عنده يضمن اليضة ولا يرد الفرخ لأنه خلق آخر سوى البيضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted in His power and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فتعالى أمره فى قدرته وعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahsanu is an apposition or the predicate of an omitted subject; it is not an adjective because a comparative noun remains indefinite despite annexation, whose second term stands in place of min.
rows.anchor: بدل أو خبر مبتدا محذوف وليس بصفة لأنه نكرة وان أضيف لأن المضاف إليه عوض من من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaliqin here means estimators or planners; the omitted taqdīran is understood from the word.
rows.anchor: المقدرين أى أحسن المقدرين تقديرا فترك ذكر الممين لدلالة الخالقين عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says the Prophet's scribe Abd Allah ibn Sad ibn Abi Sarh uttered the phrase before it was dictated; after the Prophet said to write it as revealed, he claimed he too received revelation, apostatized, fled to Mecca, and later accepted Islam at its conquest.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن عبدالله بن سعد بن أبو سرح كان يكتب للنبى عليه السلام فنطق بذلك قبل املائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi rejects that story as unsound: the apostasy occurred in Medina, whereas this sūra is Meccan.
rows.anchor: وقيل هذه الحكاية غير صحيحة لأن ارتداده كان بالمدينة وهذه السورة مكية

rows.speaker: عمر أو معاذ
rows.claim: Another report attributes the phrase to Umar or Muadh.
rows.anchor: وقيل القائل عمر أو معاذ رضى الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talfahu means to burn.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تلفح ﴾ أى تحرق ﴿ وجوههم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalihun means grimacing or frowning; the verse continues by saying that something is said to them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون ﴾ عابسون فيقال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are houses that you neither own nor inhabit.
rows.anchor: أى بيوتا لستم تملكونها ولا تسكنونها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses tastaʾnisū as asking permission and read it that way.
rows.anchor: أى تستأذنوا عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما وقد قرأبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istī'nās originally means seeking information or discovering something; the verb derives from seeing something clearly and exposed, and here means finding out whether entry is permitted.
rows.anchor: والاستئناس فى الأصل الاستعلام واستكشاف استفعال من أنس الشئ إذا أبصره ظاهرا مكشوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission may be sought by saying a tasbīḥ, takbīr, taḥmīd, or by clearing one's throat.
rows.anchor: وذلك بتسبيحة أو بتكبيرة أو بتحميدة أو بتنحنح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting is to say “Peace be upon you”; ask to enter three times, and if permission is not given, return.
rows.anchor: والتسليم أن يقول السلام عليكم أأدخل ثلاث مرات فإن أذن له والا رجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says to offer the greeting first when visitor and host meet; otherwise ask permission first.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن تلاقيا يقدم التسليم والا فالاستئذان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission and greeting are better than the pre-Islamic greeting and al-dumūr, entering without leave; people used to greet and walk in, sometimes finding a man with his wife under one blanket.
rows.anchor: والدمور وهو الدخول بغير إذن فكان الرجل من أهل الجاهلية إذا دخل بيت غيره يقول حييتم صباحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālikum refers to asking permission and offering the greeting.
rows.anchor: أى استئذان والتسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction is given so people remember, take heed, and practice the rules of asking permission.
rows.anchor: أى قيل لكم هذا لكى تذكروا وتتعظوا وتعملوا ما أمرتم به فى باب الاستئذان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In is a particle of negation.
rows.anchor: ﴾ ان نافية ﴿ إلا هزوا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking someone as a mockery means ridiculing him; the underlying construction makes him an object of mockery.
rows.anchor: اتخذه هزؤا فى معنى استهزأ به والأصل اتخذه موضع هزؤا ومهزوءا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is quoted after an omitted verb of saying and expresses contempt; an implied saying introduces the question.
rows.anchor: محكى بعد القول المضمر وهذا استصغار واستهزاء أى قائلين أهذا الذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A relative pronoun's object is omitted: the one whom God sent as a messenger.
rows.anchor: والمحذوف حال والعائد إلى الذى محذوف أى بعثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who follows desire in what they do or leave undone worships desire and makes it their god.
rows.anchor: أى من أطاع هواه فيما يأتى ويذر فهو عابد هواه وجاعله الهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asks how the Prophet could call someone who recognizes only desire as a god to guidance.
rows.anchor: هذا الذى لا يرى معبودا الا هواه كيف تستطيع ان تدعوه إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a pre-Islamic man worshipped a stone, then replaced it with a better-looking stone when he passed one.
rows.anchor: يروى أن الواحد من أهل الجاهلية كان يعبد الحجر فاذا مر بحجر أحسن منه ترك الأول وعبد الثانى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan applies the verse to every person who follows their own desire.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن هو فى كل متع هواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is no guardian commissioned to turn such a person from desire to guidance; his role is only to convey the message.
rows.anchor: أى حفيظا تحفظه من متابعة هواه وعبادة ما يهواه أفأنت تكون عليه موكلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kam is in the accusative as the object of anbatnā.
rows.anchor: كم نصب بانبتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj means a kind or species of plant.
rows.anchor: صنف من النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karīm means praiseworthy and greatly beneficial, feeding people and livestock, like a generous person whose benefit is widespread.
rows.anchor: محمود كثير المنفعة يأكل منه الناس والأنعام كالرجل الكريم الذى نفعه عام

words: كَمْ أَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining kam and kull signals both abundant number and comprehensive coverage of plant kinds, highlighting God's complete power.
rows.anchor: وفائدة الجمع بين كلمتى الكثرة والاحاطة أن كلمة كل تدل على الإحاطة بأزواج النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is the object of an implied verb: “remember when.”
rows.anchor: مفعول به أى اذكر اذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāda means that the Lord called Moses.
rows.anchor: دعا ربك موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An here means ay, introducing the content “that is: go.”
rows.anchor: ان أئت ان بمعنى أى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wronged themselves through disbelief and the Israelites through enslavement and killing their sons.
rows.anchor: أنفسهم بالكفر وبنى إسرائيل بالاستعباد وذبح الأولاد سجل عليهم بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Pharaoh's people” is an explanatory apposition, glossing the oppressive people as Pharaoh's people; both expressions denote the same group.
rows.anchor: عليهم عطف البيان كأن معنى القوم الظالمين وترجمته قوم فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an urging: go to them as an admonisher, for it is time they became Godfearing.
rows.anchor: أى ائتهم زاجرا فقد آن لهم أن يتقوا وهى كلمة حث وإغراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is circumstantial of the pronoun in “the wrongdoers”: they oppress while heedless of God and His punishment, with the interrogative hamza applied to the circumstance.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنه حال من الضمير فى الظالمين أى يظلموا غير متقين الله وعقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The act was Moses' killing of the Egyptian Copt.
rows.anchor: يعنى قتل القبطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh meant that Moses denied his favor by killing his baker.
rows.anchor: بنعمتى حيث قتلت خبازى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh meant that Moses belonged to their religion, which Pharaoh called disbelief.
rows.anchor: أو كنت على ديننا الذى تسمية كفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's charge is false: Moses was protected from unbelief and lived among them under dissimulation.
rows.anchor: وهذا افتراء منه عليه لأنه معصوم من الكفر وكان يعايشهم بالتقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun qawm can be masculine or feminine in agreement.
rows.anchor: القوم يذكر ويؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Noah was born in Adam's lifetime.
rows.anchor: قيل ولد نوح فى زمن آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The messengers” is plural although only Noah is intended, as in saying someone rides mounts or wears cloaks while owning one of each.
rows.anchor: والمراد نوح عليه السلام قولك فلان يركب الدواب ويلبس البرود وماله إلا دابة أو برد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the people rejected messengership altogether, so the plural is apt.
rows.anchor: أو كانوا ينكرون بعث الرسل أصلا فلذا جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting one messenger is rejecting all, since each messenger calls people to believe in every messenger; Nasafi says the same applies throughout this sūra.
rows.anchor: لأن من كذب واحدا منهم فقد كذب الكل لأن كل رسول يدعو الناس إلى الإيمان بجميع الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is their brother by lineage, not by religion.
rows.anchor: نسبا لا دينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls them to fear the Creator of all people and abandon idol worship.
rows.anchor: خالق الأنام فتتركوا عبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was known among his people for trustworthiness, like Muhammad among Quraysh.
rows.anchor: كان مشهورا بالأمانة فيهم كمحمد عليه الصلاة والسلام فى قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah tells them to fear God and obey him in the truth he commands and calls them to.
rows.anchor: فيما آمركم به وأدعوكم اليه من الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's sole task is to warn clearly with sound proof distinguishing truth from falsehood; the people remain responsible for their own course.
rows.anchor: ما على إلا أن أنذركم إنذارا بينا بالبرهان الصحيح الذي يتميز به الحق من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell Noah to stop what he is saying.
rows.anchor: عما تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threaten that he will be among those killed by stoning.
rows.anchor: من المقتولين بالحجارة

none: Only the quoted verse is given.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud calls his people to fear God by not rejecting the trustworthy messenger.
rows.anchor: فاتقوا الله ﴾ في تكذيب الرسول الأمين

none: Only the quoted verse is given.
Only the quoted verse is given.
Only the quoted verse is given.
Only the quoted verse is given.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min can explain the phrase “what your Lord created for you” or indicate a part of it; the intended part is the permitted sexual organ of the women.
rows.anchor: من تبيين لما خلق أو تبعيض والمراد بما خلق العضو المباح منهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people practiced this act with their wives as well.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يفعلون مثل ذلك بنسائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves that anal intercourse with wives or female slaves is forbidden; Nasafi calls anyone who permits it gravely mistaken.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على تحريم ادبار الزوجات والمملوكات ومن أجازه فقد أخطأ خطأ عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀdī means a transgressor who exceeds the limit in injustice; their grave act makes them especially deserving of that description.
rows.anchor: العادى المتعدى فى ظلمه المتجاوز فيه الحد أى بل أنتم قوم أحق بأن توصوا بالعدوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell Lot to stop condemning and reproaching their conduct.
rows.anchor: عن انكارك علينا وتقبيح أمرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threaten to expel him from among them and drive him from their town, perhaps in the harshest manner.
rows.anchor: من جملة من أخرجناه من بين أظهرنا وطردناه من بلدنا ولعلهم كانوا يخرجون من أخرجوه على أسوأ حال

none: Only the quoted verse is given.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they obey, lower your wing to them; if they disobey and do not follow, disavow them and their deeds, including shirk and anything else they do.
rows.anchor: فإن اتبعوك وأطاعوك فاخفض جناحك لهم وإن عصوك ولم يتبعوك فتبرأ منهم ومن أعمالهم من الشرك بالله وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God defeats the Prophet's enemies through might and helps him by mercy, shielding him from harm by those who disobey or others.
rows.anchor: على الذى يقهر أعداءك بعزته وينصرك عليهم برحمته يكفك شر من يعصيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawakkul is entrusting one's affairs to the one who controls them and can bring benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: والتوكل تفويض الرجل أمره إلى من يملك أمره ويقدر على نفعه وضره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the person who relies on God does not try to repel a crisis by disobeying Him.
rows.anchor: وقالوا المتوكل من إذا دهمه أمر لم يحاول دفعه عن نفسه بما هو معصية لله

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd defines reliance as turning wholly toward God and wholly away from all else, since one's need is for Him in both abodes.
rows.anchor: وقال الجنيدر رضى الله عنه التوكل ان تقبل بالكلية على ربك وتعرض بالكلية عما دونه

rows.speaker: مدني وشامي
rows.claim: Madinan and Shami read fa-tawakkal; it is coordinated either with fa-qul or with fa-lā tadʿu.
rows.anchor: فتوكل مدنى وشامى عطف على فقل أو فلا تدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is seen when he rises for night prayer.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذي يراك حين تقوم ﴾ متهجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqallub means God's seeing the Prophet's movement among those who pray.
rows.anchor: فى المصلين أتبع كونه رحيما على رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This follows the mention of God's mercy: the Prophet prayed in the night and discreetly checked on his companions' worship and work for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أتبع كونه رحيما على رسوله ما هو من أسباب الرحمة وهو ذكر ما كان يفعله فى جوف الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means the Prophet's movement among worshippers as he led them in congregational prayer, standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه يراك حين تقوم للصلاة بالناس جماعة وتقلبه فى الساجدين تصرفه فيما بينهم بقيامه وركوعه وسجوده وقعوده

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil asked Abu Hanifa whether congregational prayer is mentioned in the Qur'an; Abu Hanifa said he could not recall it, so Muqatil recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن مقاتل أنه سأل أبا حنيفة هل تجد الصلاة بالجماعة فى القرآن فقال لا يحضرنى فتلاله هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thing Moses came to was the fire he had seen.
rows.anchor: أي النار التي أبصرها نودى موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An may be the lightened form of anna: “he was called that blessed [is]”; the pronoun denotes the matter at hand. Although al-Zamakhshari disallows this without a compensating particle, the construction is permitted because a prayer has special rules.
rows.anchor: مخففة من الثقيلة وتقديره نودى بأن بورك والضمير ضمير الشان وجاز ذلك من غير عوض وإن منعه الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an is explanatory because the call carries the sense of speech.
rows.anchor: ومفسرة لأن في النداء معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Būrika means “was sanctified” or “was endowed with blessing and goodness.”
rows.anchor: أي قدس أو جعل فيه البركة والخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in the place of the fire are the angels; the one around it is Moses, since a religious event occurred there: God spoke to and commissioned him and showed him miracles.
rows.anchor: أي بورك من في مكان النار وهم الملائكة ومن حول مكانها أي موسى لحدوث أمر ديني فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These words are part of the call and declare God transcendent of likeness and anything else unworthy of Him.
rows.anchor: هو من جملة ما نودي فقد نزه ذاته عما لا يليق به من التشبيه وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is told to throw his staff so he will recognize the miracle and find reassurance in it; the command is coordinated with the blessing pronouncement.
rows.anchor: لتعلم معجزتك فتأنس بها وهو عطف على بورك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the blessing and throwing the staff explain what Moses was called to hear; al-Qasas puts the command after the call to Moses, repeating the explanatory particle.
rows.anchor: لأن المعنى نودى أن بورك من في النار وأن ألق عصاك كلاهما تفسير لنودى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahtazzu is a circumstantial clause attached to the object pronoun in raʾāhā.
rows.anchor: تتحرك حال من الهاء في رآها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jan is a small snake.
rows.anchor: حية صغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase as though it were a small snake is a circumstantial clause of the pronoun in tahtazzu.
rows.anchor: حال من الضمير في تهتز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses turned away and fled, putting his back to the snake out of fear that it would spring on him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولي ﴾ موسى ﴿ مدبرا ﴾ أدبر عنها وجعلها تلى ظهره خوفا من ثوب الحية عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam yuʿaqqib means he did not look back or did not return; the idiom can describe someone who returns to fight after fleeing.
rows.anchor: ولم يلتفت أو لم يرجع يقال قد عقب فلان إذا رجع يقاتل بعد أن ولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense is that messengers do not fear while God is addressing them.
rows.anchor: أي لا يخاف عندي المرسلون حال خطابي اياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, messengers do not fear anyone besides God.
rows.anchor: أو لا يخاف لدى المرسلون من غيري
